headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and data-leakage via AutoGPT’s filesystem/CLI outputs into marker’s document-processing workflow; no direct shared-channel evidence lowers confidence.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and use the filesystem, so it can emit attacker-controlled content into files or CLI output. marker is a document-processing agent with no read_filesystem or use_mcp capability shown, so a direct default bridge is not documented. Because the interaction is inferred rather than evidenced, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF AutoGPT writes prompt-like text into a file that marker later ingests
IF an external orchestrator copies AutoGPT output into marker input without sanitization
mitigations: Restrict AutoGPT outputs to structured JSON only
Disable file handoff between agents
Add a provenance tag to every transferred document
Require marker to ignore instruction-like text in inputs
requires-engineering: add content filtering at the handoff boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted network egress, while marker has no network egress and no filesystem read/write capability listed. No sensitive data classes are declared for either agent, so a leakage path is possible only through unusual shared-file workflows and the blast radius appears limited. The pairwise risk is therefore low, not medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory
IF AutoGPT is given secrets or sensitive documents to process
mitigations: Keep agents on separate workspaces
Do not place secrets in AutoGPT inputs
Mount marker input as read-only
Review AutoGPT egress allowlist
requires-engineering: add per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can write via filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but marker is explicitly unable to write_filesystem, modify_git_state, or spawn_subprocesses. That removes the main shared-write conflict pathway. Any contention would require external orchestration or unusual permissions not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF an external wrapper grants marker write access not shown in its profile
IF both agents are manually pointed at the same mutable git repository
mitigations: Keep marker read-only
Avoid shared git worktrees
Run AutoGPT in a separate directory
Serialize any file writes through one owner
requires-engineering: add lockfiles for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate outputs from shell and filesystem activity, and marker is a document-processing system that may transform those outputs. There is no evidence marker verifies provenance or independently checks AutoGPT claims, so A-to-B propagation is plausible in default document pipelines. Because the handoff is inferred, not documented, medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF marker consumes AutoGPT-produced documents as authoritative source text
IF no human or automated verification step is inserted between them
mitigations: Insert a verification step before marker processes AutoGPT output
Require citations for any factual claims
Separate draft and final document stages
Flag unverified AutoGPT text as non-authoritative
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware routing

E_compliance.rationale: Neither profile declares regulated data classes, residency constraints, certifications, or retention policies. AutoGPT and marker are both open-source and the profiles do not show a compliance mismatch pathway. With no declared compliance-sensitive data flow, a residency or certification breach is not evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later assigned to either agent
IF a deployment policy imposes residency or retention requirements not present in the profiles
mitigations: Document data-class handling before deployment
Avoid routing regulated data through the pair
Add retention policy checks
Review residency requirements
requires-engineering: implement compliance gating
